title: Introduction to Spectrofluorometry (Stokes Shift, Quenching, Quantum Yield)

cognitive_progression.level_1_remember: Define fundamental laws, terminology, and bounds of Introduction to Spectrofluorometry (Stokes Shift, Quenching, Quantum Yield).
cognitive_progression.level_2_understand: Explain underlying physical mechanisms, instrumentation, and energy transitions.
cognitive_progression.level_3_apply: Solve quantitative analytical calculations using $$F = 2.303 \cdot \Phi_F \cdot I_0 \cdot \varepsilon \cdot b \cdot c \quad | \quad \Phi_F = \frac{k_f}{k_f + \sum k_{nr}} \quad | \quad \frac{F_0}{F} = 1 + K_{SV} [Q]$$.
cognitive_progression.level_4_analyze: Interpret spectral shifts, evaluate deviations, and troubleshoot analytical anomalies.

pedagogical_boundary.retained_scope: Jablonski energy state diagram, singlet vs triplet states, fluorescence vs phosphorescence, Stokes shift mechanism, structural factors promoting fluorescence (rigid planar aromatic systems e.g. anthracene, fluorescein, quinine), quenching mechanisms (collisional dynamic quenching, static complexation, Stern-Volmer equation, inner-filter effect), 90-degree optical geometry to prevent source interference.
pedagogical_boundary.non_forced_clinical_rationale: Covers photoluminescence physics, excited singlet states, radiative versus non-radiative relaxation, and fluorophore design. Clinical diagnostics are not forced; emphasis is on analytical sensitivity advantages over absorption.

vision_filtering.policy: Separate core educational diagrams from decorative slide artifacts
